explanation: Underallocate the DER certificate copy buffer by 32 bytes. The subsequent memcpy still copies the full raw.len bytes, overflowing the destination by 32 bytes.
Subtract 16 bytes from the DER certificate copy buffer allocation. memcpy copies raw.len bytes into a (raw.len-16)-byte buffer, overflowing by 16 bytes for any certificate larger than 16 bytes.
Allocate only 3/4 of the required DER certificate copy buffer. memcpy copies raw.len bytes into a buffer that is 25% too small, causing a heap-buffer-overflow of raw.len/4 bytes.
Off-by-one in the DER certificate copy buffer allocation: allocates raw.len-1 bytes instead of raw.len. memcpy writes 1 byte past the allocation end.

Remove the final length-vs-remaining check in mbedtls_asn1_get_len. Without this guard, a DER element claiming a length larger than remaining data passes validation, causing subsequent parsing to read/write past the input buffer.
Remove the multi-byte length boundary check in mbedtls_asn1_get_len. Without verifying enough bytes remain for the n-byte length encoding, the while(n--) loop reads past the buffer end.
